objections.claim: D-028 and D-029 no longer state what their own Route B selection buys. This turn's compression removed the clause defining what a completed disposition may discharge and within what scope, plus the sentence preserving conditions 2 through 5, from exactly those two entries — leaving two self-contained entries that select a route without stating its effect.
objections.evidence: Normalized across line wrapping, 'may discharge condition 1' occurs 5 times in the turn-1 draft (cd9f8f86) and 3 times in the turn-2 draft (05f90556). The three survivors are at turn-2 lines 157 (D-026, DR-002), 216 (D-027, DR-004) and 401 (D-030, DR-003). D-028 and D-029 are the two that lost it. Turn-1 D-028 §5 read: 'This entry writes no disposition, marks nothing SATISFIED, and authorizes no blueprint. A completed, reviewed disposition recorded by the owning authority may discharge condition 1 for DR-005 within the preview scope it names. Conditions 2–5 remain independently required. Condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/.' Turn-2 D-028 §5 reads in full: 'Writes no disposition. Marks nothing SATISFIED. Authorizes no blueprint.' D-029 §5 is identical in form and suffered the same loss. Separately, 'Condition 5 remains the only authorization' occurs 4 times in turn 1 and 0 times in turn 2. This matters because self-containment is this cycle's organizing premise: if D-028 alone is adopted, it selects Route B for DR-005 and never says that a completed disposition discharges condition 1 within the named scope, nor that conditions 2 through 5 survive. Every sibling selector still says both or one of them, so the draft's own convention is to state it and two entries silently depart from it.
objections.proposedFix: Restore to D-028 §5 and D-029 §5 the two sentences retained by D-026, D-027 and D-030: the discharge-scope clause naming the row, and 'Conditions 2–5 remain independently required.' Restoring 'Condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/' to all five selectors would also return that statement to the draft, where it currently appears nowhere.

objections.claim: D-025 carries no rationale element and no stated basis for its RULE-GOVERNED classification. D-000 clause 3 requires rationale of every entry, and this entry's decision type was the contested question that opened the terminated cycle.
objections.evidence: D-000 clause 3: 'Every such decision is documented in this register — decision, alternatives, RATIONALE, reviewer verdict with digest, reversibility class, overturn procedure.' D-025's decision-type line reads, in full, 'Decision type: RULE-GOVERNED.' It supplies no basis. The six preference-laden entries each carry an 'Honesty about the trade' paragraph that serves as rationale; D-025 is RULE-GOVERNED so it correctly has none, but nothing replaces it, making D-025 the only entry in the draft with no rationale element at all. The omission is pointed rather than incidental because the RULE-GOVERNED label on this entry's ancestor was the terminated cycle's first MUST-FIX (a closed consumption set called a restatement), and the defense then was an explicit enumeration: the CONTESTED D-017 read 'RULE-GOVERNED. This entry restates rules already present in file 08's only-active-checklist paragraph, file 07's and file 10's competing-list disclaimers, file 11's own header, and D-001's three closure routes. It adds no fourth route and no new closed consumption set.' That enumeration is gone. The label is also load-bearing: RULE-GOVERNED entries are exempt from D-000 clause 5's preference marking and cheaper-overturn requirement.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the basis sentence to D-025's decision-type line, naming the sources it restates and asserting that it adds no fourth route and no new closed set — a claim the turn-2 text now genuinely supports.

objections.claim: The D-025 to D-031 coupling tightened this turn rather than loosening. D-031's accounting dropped the half of D-025 Decision 4 that does the operative work, does not list D-025 among its dependencies, and D-025 claims unqualified total reversibility despite having a live dependent — so reverting C-D025 would strand D-031's accounting rule.
objections.evidence: Three measured limbs. First, turn-1 D-031's accounting read 'Per D-025 Decision 4, inclusion here is authorization to draft, not live work. SUBSTANTIVE OUTCOMES REMAIN OPEN UNTIL THE DRAFTED ARTIFACT TRAVELS A, B, OR C.' Turn-2 reads 'Per D-025 Decision 4, inclusion here is authorization to draft, not live work.' and stops. 'Substantive outcomes remain open' occurs once in the turn-1 draft and zero times in turn 2. At turn 1 I recorded the coupling as a NOTE precisely because the rule was restated inline; it no longer is, so D-031's accounting is now a bare citation to a severable sibling. Second, D-031's header declares 'Depends on, but is severable from: D-018 (ADOPTED) and D-026..D-030 (if adopted)' — D-025 is absent from that list although the accounting section depends on it. Third, D-025's overturn reads 'Reversibility class: total. Overturn: supersession plus git revert of C-D025', with no temporal boundary, while all five selectors received exactly such a boundary this turn for the weaker case of dispositions that do not yet exist. D-025 has a dependent in the same draft.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the second sentence to D-031's accounting so the rule is stated in full there; add D-025 to D-031's dependency line; and give D-025 the same temporal reversibility boundary the selectors carry, naming D-031 as the dependent whose accounting must be superseded or reverted alongside it.

objections.claim: Two further statements lost substance to compression this turn. Neither is false; both were more informative one draft ago, and both belong to the class of losses already raised at C2N2-D028-01 and C2N2-BOTH-01.
objections.evidence: First, the closing list item read 'Do not skip TM; D-030 selects a scoped model, not an absence' in the turn-1 draft and reads 'Do not skip TM' in turn 2. The clarifier that distinguished scoping from waiving — the distinction the whole DR-003 treatment turns on — is gone from the summary list, though D-030 §4 still carries it. Second, turn-1 D-031 read 'Condition-2/4 sets continue per D-001 SF-3 over the register as it stands at readiness evaluation, including rows added by later recorded acts'; turn 2 reads 'Condition-2/4 sets continue per D-001 SF-3.' The phrase 'over the register as it stands' occurs once in turn 1 and zero times in turn 2. The compressed form is accurate as a citation, but the affirmative statement it replaced was itself the repair for the terminated cycle's C2-D018-02, where the defect was a rule constraining when those sets may be recalculated. A bare citation restores the reader's dependence on reading SF-3 elsewhere.
objections.proposedFix: Restore both qualifiers. Neither costs more than a clause, and both were written in response to earlier findings in this lineage.
